run.change_description:
commit-c3a3d1c: Update conn state to prevent concurrent connection attempts

commit-6214c9d: Make callers of resetBackoff() lock the mutex

commit-ff977b3: Add doc comment for resetTransportAndUnlock

commit-76ef33f: Merge remote-tracking branch 'source/master' into fix_conn_connect_race

summary.intent: Close the race where addrConn.connect() released ac.mu before calling resetTransport(), letting a second connect() call see the Idle state and start a duplicate connection attempt; keep the mutex held from the Idle check through the transition to Connecting so no second attempt can start.
summary.issue_fit: Met — the change addresses the double-connection-attempt race the linked issue's root-cause comment traces to addrConn.connect() releasing ac.mu before calling resetTransport().
summary.coverage: The single changed file, clientconn.go, is reviewed in full: connect(), updateAddrs(), and the renamed resetTransportAndUnlock() were traced against every caller in the repository.
check_details: go vet . at the same head: clean, no diagnostics.
go test -race -run 'Test/SubConnEmpty' ./test: pass; exercises UpdateAddresses transitioning through TransientFailure, not the Ready-with-active-transport branch the finding below concerns.
The reported 100000-attempt flake measurement was not reproduced; it exceeds the bounded, offline focused-test allowance.

findings.title: Release ac.mu before spawning the reconnect goroutine in updateAddrs
findings.trigger: updateAddrs takes the branch where an active transport exists and the addresses changed: it defers ac.transport.GracefulClose(), sets ac.transport = nil, then calls go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock() without unlocking ac.mu first.
findings.impact: When updateAddrs returns, the deferred GracefulClose() runs on the same goroutine and its onClose closure calls ac.mu.Lock(); since ac.mu is still held, only handed to the freshly spawned goroutine, that call now blocks until the new goroutine's setup runs and releases it — a wait base code never had, since it unlocked before spawning.
findings.change: Call ac.mu.Unlock() before go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock() in updateAddrs; unlike connect()'s Idle check, this branch never runs when ac.state is Idle, so releasing the lock here does not reopen the race this change fixes.
findings.source: spec-pr7390-packet/thread-comment/arjan-bal/"ac.updateAddrs calls resetTransport in a new go routine so it can't hold the lock till resetTransport completes... I feel we could end up in a situation where the lock is not released correctly resulting in a deadlock."

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/pr-body/"keep holding the mutex instead of releasing it and having resetTransport() re-acquire it"
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go: connect() (line 922) and updateAddrs() (line 996) no longer call ac.mu.Unlock() before invoking resetTransportAndUnlock(), and resetTransportAndUnlock() (line 1234) no longer re-locks.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/pr-body/"no concurrent requests are able to start once caller of resetTransport does some validation and calls resetTransport"
requirements.evidence: connect() holds ac.mu from the Idle check through resetTransportAndUnlock()'s transition to Connecting (clientconn.go:906-922, 1234-1263), closing the window a concurrent connect() call previously used to also observe Idle.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/pr-body/"RELEASE NOTES: - client: fix race that could lead to orphaned connections and associated resources."
requirements.evidence: Preventing the duplicate resetTransport invocation removes the mechanism the issue thread traced to orphaned transports: only one of two concurrently created transports was ever tracked in ac.transport.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/thread-comment/dfawley/"ac.mu must be held by the caller, and this function will guarantee it is released."
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:1231-1233 carries this exact doc comment on resetTransportAndUnlock.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390-packet/pr-body/"Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts with the change."
requirements.evidence: The reported 0.4% flake rate cannot be confirmed or refuted by a bounded, offline focused run, and the AuthorityRevive scenario was not re-run; the fix mechanism was verified directly instead (see the first two requirement rows) and the affected package's existing addrConn/backoff unit tests pass with the race detector at head.
